question: why does the pipeline split conductors on the 25 circuits a frontier model recovers
conclusions: Notching is NOT the cause of the recoverable splits: only 4% of those circuits contain a detected crossover, against 53% of the hard core. The two failure populations are separated by crossover presence as well as by split-vs-fusion.

Ink availability is comparable across all three groups (0.021-0.027 of pixels), so the split population is not fainter. The pipeline retains a smaller fraction of the ink it has (0.538 against 0.655 on circuits it solves) and fragments the remainder into 14.5 mask components against 8.1.

That places the cause inside wire-mask construction - binarization, blob filtering, and masking - which is the self-inflicted-damage class that every successful fix in this project has belonged to, and not the inference class that every failed attempt has belonged to.
